chart.$description:
Chart plot geometry. Script-readable: JS arithmetic must consume these
to produce an SVG position, and no CSS expression can compute a y attribute
from a data value. They are emitted to both targets (the custom property and
the per-layer JS module), so they still appear in the Overview. Accepted cost:
a value bound at import time cannot re-densify, so chart geometry does not
respond to .arena-compact. It never did.

pad-top.$description: The plot's top padding, one step of the base grid.

pad-right.$description: The plot's right padding, one step of the base grid.

pad-bottom.$description:
Holds the category labels. This is a CONSEQUENCE of the type scale, not a
chosen dimension: it is enough room for a label at --dz-text-xs, which is the step a
category label takes because a name under a plot is chrome and not prose. If the type
scale moves, revisit it; it will not fail loudly.
The labels stay on this edge whatever the data does, so a bar growing down from a
zero line above the floor runs toward them. That is deliberate: a reader looks for
category labels along the bottom, and moving them to follow the zero line would put
them somewhere different in every chart on a page. What it costs is a downward bar
reaching its label at the extreme of the axis, which is the price of one place to
look.

pad-category.$description:
Holds the category names down the left edge of a horizontal bar chart, where
pad-left holds value labels on a vertical one. A separate token rather than a wider
pad-left, because the two hold different things and sizing every chart's value gutter for
the longest category name anyone might write would waste 52px on every vertical chart in
the library. A CONSEQUENCE of the type scale like pad-bottom, and a soft one: a name longer
than it fits is truncated rather than overrunning the plot, so this is the width at which a
reader stops needing the tooltip to read a label, not a limit on what may be passed.

pad-left.$description: Holds the value labels. A consequence of the type scale, like pad-bottom.

label-gap.$description:
Between an axis label and the plot it labels: a y-axis tick label ends this far
left of pad-left, and an x-axis category label sits this far above the bottom
edge. It is a spacing decision, so it is a token by the same criterion the pads
are.

tick-char.$description:
The advance of one character of a tick label, which is what lets the axis measure
its widest tick without a DOM to ask. A CONSEQUENCE of two decisions rather than a
chosen dimension: a tick is written in the mono face, whose advance is 0.6em, at
--dz-text-2xs, which is 10px in both densities. Measured in the browser at 6.0016px
and rounded down to the whole pixel, because the gutter takes the ceiling of what it
computes and a hundredth of a pixel per character is not room anybody can see. It
holds only while the ticks stay monospaced: a proportional face makes a label's width
its glyphs' business and no arithmetic can answer it.

ring-inset.$description:
Breathing room between the doughnut's outer radius and its box, so a slice's
stroke is not clipped. Not a multiplier deriving one dimension from another --
those stay inline by the recorded criterion -- but a chosen gap, which is why
this one is a token and the 0.62 inner-radius ratio beside it is not.

bar-radius.$description:
A bar's data end. Deliberately NOT --r-sm (6px): naming the value Arena
already renders is free, snapping to the radius scale is a visible 2px design
change and must be taken as one.

series-gap.$description:
Between two bars of the same category, when a chart draws more than one series.
Distinct from bar-gap, which is between categories, and deliberately smaller than it:
the wider gap is what tells a reader where one category ends, and if the two were equal
a grouped chart would read as one long row of unrelated bars. Script-readable, because
JS subtracts it from a sub-band width to produce an SVG x.

point-r.$description: A line chart's point at rest.

point-r-hover.$description:
A line chart's point under the pointer. The 1px delta IS the hover
affordance: the pair only means anything together.

tooltip-offset.$description:
Between the mark under the pointer and the tooltip's near edge. Not script-readable:
the chart interpolates the mark's own y into a calc() and CSS subtracts this from it, so
the stylesheet is what consumes the token. It settles a disagreement rather than recording
one: the bar chart offset its tooltip by --sp-2 and the line chart by 2.5 steps of --sp-1,
which is 10px against 8px for the same affordance. Naming it moves the line chart's tooltip
2px, and that is a visible design change taken deliberately, the same way chart.bar-radius
refuses to snap to --r-sm because doing so would be one.

bubble-r-min.$description:
A bubble at the smallest value it carries. Equals point-r, deliberately: a bubble
chart with one size in it is a scatter, and it should draw like one rather than jumping to
some other mark size the moment a third column appears.

bubble-r-max.$description:
A bubble at the largest value it carries. The pair is a RADIUS range and the
mapping between them is by area, not by radius: doubling a radius quadruples the blot, and a
reader compares the blot, so a linear radius exaggerates the large value by a factor of four.
Sixteen is what fits the size key beside the series names without either crowding the other,
and it is a chosen dimension rather than a consequence, unlike the pads.

legend-gap.$description: Between the doughnut plot and its legend.

legend-strip.$description:
The row of series keys a cartesian chart draws below its plot, height including
the separation from the plot. A CONSEQUENCE of the type scale rather than a chosen
dimension, the way pad-bottom is: one line at --dz-text-sm stands 18px at the root line
height, the swatch beside it is smaller and rides inside that line, and one step of the base
grid separates the row from the plot. If the type scale moves, revisit it; it will not fail
loudly.
It comes OUT of the plot rather than being added to the chart's box, so --chart-height stays
the height of the whole component whether a legend is drawn or not. That is the same trade
the doughnut already makes on the other axis, where the legend column takes its width from
the ring rather than from the caller.
